function: p. 1, 4: Joint device activity detection and channel estimation from pilots in grant-free MIMO-OFDM access; a learned score-based channel prior acts as MMSE denoiser inside turbo message passing.
system: p. 3, 11: Uplink grant-free MIMO-OFDM; BS with 32-antenna ULA, single-antenna devices, K=800 devices, 48 subcarriers, 2.6 GHz; no RIS.
method: p. 8-11: First- and second-order score networks (NCSNv2/NCSN, U-Net/RefineNet CNNs), unsupervised denoising score matching on channel samples, plugged into model-based turbo message passing; no per-scenario retraining.
data_channel: p. 11: QuaDRiGa-generated 3GPP TR 38.901 CDL channels; 50,000 training samples with randomized CDL-C path angles, delays and gains; 5,000 evaluation samples directly from CDL-C.
test_conditions: p. 11-14: Trained at SNR -10 to 30 dB on randomized CDL-C; tested on CDL-C with varied K, activity, pilot length, Hadamard pilots, and on CDL-B, without retraining.
baselines: p. 12-13: Non-learned message passing BG-TMP, GMMV-AMP, TMP-EM; denoiser baselines LS, OMP, element-wise MMSE, VALSE, genie-aided lower bound; no learned neural baseline.
metrics: p. 11-14: Channel-estimation NMSE versus iteration, SNR, number of devices K, activity probability, pilot length; activity detection error probability (misses plus false alarms); convergence speed; training-set size.
complexity: p. 11-12: Per-iteration complexity O(MNK log2 K + C) complex multiplications, C being the score-network forward-pass cost; training takes about one day per network; converges in 10-20 iterations.
q1_support: p. 11: "We adopt the CDL family of channel models generated from the QuaDRiGa toolbox [55] for training and evaluation." The evaluation samples come from CDL-C of [32], which is 3GPP TR 38.901 (reference list, p. 15).
q2_support: p. 14: "the score networks are trained on the CDL-C dataset, while the STMP-JADCE algorithm is evaluated on the distinct CDL-B channel model."
q3_support: p. 12: "We compare the proposed STMP-JADCE algorithm against the following baselines" BG-TMP, GMMV-AMP and TMP-EM, which p. 13 calls "model-based baselines". Missing: no earlier learned (neural) JADCE or channel estimator is compared, although deep unfolding and LSTM methods are cited on p. 3.
q4_support: p. 11: "the overall per-iteration complexity of STMP-JADCE is O (M N K log2 K + C)", with C the cost of the score-network forward passes.
q5_support: p. 11: "directly generated from the CDL-C model specified in [32, Table 7.7.1-3]"; the authors generate their own samples with the QuaDRiGa toolbox, and no code or dataset link or DOI is given anywhere in the paper.
notes: Area 2 because the main metric is the channel NMSE (pp. 11-14). Activity detection here is pilot-based detection at the receiver (p. 4), not an access-control or scheduling decision, so it is not above_phy. TMP-EM learns its prior variance online with EM (p. 12), which is not counted as a learned baseline, so q3 is 0 and the reviewer may revisit it. QuaDRiGa is a channel generator, not a released dataset, so q5 is 0.
